## Problem
During parent/epic implementation, `implement.py finish <child>` pushes the child's feature branch to `refs/heads/dev` on the remote but does NOT fast-forward (or otherwise update) the local `dev` branch. The next `implement.py parent <epic>` call creates the next child's worktree from the stale local `dev`, so the new worktree is missing the just-merged sibling's files.

## Observed
- F2 (AH-0MUBYU600004YU4T) finish pushed commit 91538d0 to origin/dev; local dev stayed at 1920e65.
- The F3 worktree (AH-0MUBYXR280018HST) was created from local dev 1920e65 and could not resolve `../powerups/collectAnimation` (added by F2) until local dev was fast-forwarded to origin/dev and merged into the worktree.

## Impact
Every child after the first can be created from a stale base, causing phantom build errors and risking lost/duplicated work. Workaround applied manually during the parent AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W run.

## Suggested fix
After a successful push in `phase_finish`, fast-forward the local parent branch to the pushed tip when the main checkout's parent branch is clean/unchanged (or at minimum, document the required manual `git fetch && git merge --ff-only origin/dev` step).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `implement.py finish` leaves local `dev` at least as advanced as the tip it pushed (when safe to fast-forward).
- [ ] A regression test covers the local-parent-branch update after a successful push.
- [ ] `implement.py parent` creates each child worktree from the up-to-date base.

discovered-from:AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W
data.title: implement.py finish leaves local dev behind after pushing to remote dev

# Player-death juice parameter model and constants

## Goal
Provide the pure, testable foundation for the player-death "juice": a single
`resolveJuiceParams(severity)` mapping and all tunable constants in one module
(`src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`), so the rendering layers and scene wiring stay thin.

## User story
As a developer/designer tuning feel, I can change shake intensity, flash alpha,
debris/shockwave counts and severity multipliers in one module, and the exported
parameter model is covered by unit tests so tuning does not silently regress.

## Scope
- New module `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` exporting:
  - `PlayerDeathSeverity = 'respawn' | 'fatal'`.
  - `interface PlayerDeathJuiceParams` (shake intensity/duration, flash
    alpha/duration/colour, debris count/lifespan, shockwave radius/duration,
    per-layer enabled flags, particle count/lifespan/scale overrides).
  - `resolveJuiceParams(severity): PlayerDeathJuiceParams` — pure, total,
    deterministic; unknown severity falls back to `'respawn'` (never throws).
  - Exported tunable constants in one module: `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_INTENSITY`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHAKE_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_ALPHA`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_DURATION_MS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_FLASH_COLOR`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_COUNT`, `PLAYER_DEATH_DEBRIS_LIFESPAN_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_RADIUS`, `PLAYER_DEATH_SHOCKWAVE_DURATION_MS`,
    `PLAYER_DEATH_SEVERITY_*` multipliers, and `PLAYER_DEATH_ENABLE_*` toggles.
- Tests `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` written FIRST (test-first spec).

## Constraints
- Parameter logic is pure: **no Phaser import** in the parameter model.
- Colours centre on `SHIP_COLOR` (0x00ffff) per GDD §7.1.
- Intake assumptions: shake duration ~250–400 ms, intensity ~0.008–0.02,
  flash duration ~120–200 ms; keep values inside those bounds.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ intake brief (AC2, AC4, AC5).
- Predecessor: AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` constants style).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.test.ts` exists and was written before the implementation; it fails against the pre-change tree.
- [ ] `resolveJuiceParams('respawn')` and `resolveJuiceParams('fatal')` return complete `PlayerDeathJuiceParams` with every field populated.
- [ ] Every asserted `'fatal'` magnitude is strictly greater than the corresponding `'respawn'` magnitude (shake intensity + duration, flash alpha, debris count, shockwave radius).
- [ ] All tunables are exported constants from the single module; no magic numbers remain in the helper.
- [ ] Unknown/invalid severity returns the `'respawn'` parameter set and never throws.
- [ ] `npm test` passes (including the new suite) and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] Covers parent AC5 — severity scaling & no behaviour change: the effect is heavier and every tunable is an exported constant.
data.title: Player-death juice parameter model and constants

# Dedicated player-destruction SFX

## Goal
Add `playPlayerDestructionSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts` — a heavier, layered,
player-specific cue distinct from the generic enemy `playDestructionSound()` —
plus unit tests. Wiring into scenes is a separate task that depends on the
composed juice helper.

## User story
As a player, losing my ship plays a distinct low "hull breach" boom instead of
the generic enemy pop, so a life lost reads differently from a kill.

## Scope
- New exported `playPlayerDestructionSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts`, built
  from the existing Web Audio helpers (`blip`) — no new binary assets.
  Proposed layers `[ASSUMPTION]`: (1) low impact thump, (2) descending body
  sweep, (3) short filtered-noise tail. Amplitude/length exposed as exported
  constants (e.g. `PLAYER_DESTRUCTION_*`).
- Extend `src/audio/effects.test.ts` with unit tests.

## Constraints
- Synthesis via Web Audio only; no asset pipeline.
- Must never throw when audio is unavailable (mirror existing safe patterns).
- Volume within the existing player-cue ceiling and documented.
- Do NOT modify `playDestructionSound()` behaviour (enemy + shield-absorb paths
  keep it).

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZ (AC3); GDD §7.3 Audio Direction.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` `blip()` and existing per-entity cues
  (`playTankDestructionSound`, `playDiverDestructionSound`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `playPlayerDestructionSound()` is exported from `src/audio/effects.ts` and is callable without an AudioContext without throwing.
- [ ] The cue is layered (≥ 2 oscillator blips) and its amplitude/length come from exported constants, not inline literals.
- [ ] Unit tests in `src/audio/effects.test.ts` assert layer count, constant-driven amplitude/duration, and that the cue differs from `playDestructionSound()` parameters.
- [ ] `playDestructionSound()` is unchanged (its existing tests still pass).
- [ ] `npm test` passes and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] Covers parent AC3 — dedicated player-death SFX: a new playPlayerDestructionSound() is called exactly once.

# Problem

When auditing a parent/epic whose children have stored audits, the audit runner's parent-first flow (SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F) can block the parent on child verdicts that were never actually produced.

## Root cause

1. A child's audit freshness fingerprint (`_compute_content_fingerprint`) includes the git HEAD sha. Any new commit on `dev` (even unrelated) invalidates every child's stored audit, so `_child_content_changed` returns True for all children.
2. In the default in-main-slot mode (`child_in_main_slot=True`, SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE), the child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis run are emitted as `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking agent session and are left `partial` ("pending main-session review").
3. When the runner is launched non-interactively (e.g. by a downtime worker / shell subprocess), no session services that work, so every child's `ac_results` stay `partial`. `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even though all of the parent's own ACs are met/adjusted.
4. The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes the parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete`.

## Observed

During AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO (Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic into a shared core scene base class), the parent's own ACs were all met/adjusted (AC8 met via `--green-run HEAD`) and the full suite was green (75 files / 1545 tests), yet the parent audit returned "No" solely because all eight children were re-screened in-main-slot and left pending. Running with `--no-child-in-main-slot` instead hit intermittent local-proxy stalls (child screens timing out at the 600 s `--child-screen-timeout` → `partial`).

## Impact

- A passing parent audit cannot be recorded for an epic whose children were previously audited, whenever HEAD has advanced, in a non-interactive audit run.
- The parent/children statuses are demoted as a side effect of the "No" restore path.

## Suggested directions (not prescriptive)

- Make the child freshness fingerprint independent of the global HEAD sha, or scope it to the child's own key files/commits, so unrelated HEAD movement does not force a full child re-audit.
- In in-main-slot mode, treat non-serviced child verdicts as "not assessed" (inherit parent pass or mark reusable) rather than blocking the parent, or auto-fall-back to the separate-process path with retry.
- Surface a clear diagnostic distinguishing "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" from a genuine not-ready child.
data.title: Audit: parent-first flow re-audits stale children and blocks on unserviced in-main-slot verdicts

# Hold-full Power-up Choice Dialog — Opaque Backdrop

## Problem Statement

The `MineralChoiceScene` overlay (shown when the ship's mineral hold fills and the player must choose a power-up) currently uses a translucent black backdrop (`alpha: 0.75`), allowing the paused game field to remain visible behind the dialog. The requirement is for the backdrop to be fully opaque, blanking out the entire screen behind the choice dialog.

## Users

- **Player** — When the hold fills, the choice dialog should be clearly visually separated from the gameplay field by a fully black screen, improving focus on the choice options.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Opaque backdrop** — The `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA` constant in `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` is set to `1.0` (fully opaque), replacing the current value of `0.75`.
2. **Visual result** — When `MineralChoiceScene` is displayed, the entire screen behind the choice options is solid black (no transparency).
3. **No visual regressions** — The power-up choice text and option labels remain clearly readable and unchanged in appearance.
4. **All tests pass** — The full project test suite passes, including `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`.

## Constraints

- This is a minimal, surgical change: only the backdrop alpha value is modified.
- No API changes, no new parameters, no behavioural changes to choice selection logic.
- The fix applies to both the main game (`PlayScene` → `MineralChoiceScene`) and the gym scenes where the choice overlay may be launched.

## Existing State

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` defines `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA = 0.75` on line ~40.
- The backdrop is drawn as a full-screen black rectangle: `this.add.rectangle(0, 0, GAME_WIDTH, GAME_HEIGHT, 0x000000, CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA)`.
- The comment above the constant describes it as "Translucent backdrop so the paused field remains visible behind."

## Desired Change

- Set `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA` to `1.0`.
- Update the comment to reflect the opaque/blanked-out behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — Change `CHOICE_BACKDROP_ALPHA` from `0.75` to `1.0` and update its comment.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — Verify existing tests pass (no test changes expected; the backdrop alpha is not directly tested).

## Related Work

- **AH-0MUCST52T003AX4V** — "Choice modal scene and PlayScene mineral wiring" (parent feature that created this scene).
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — "Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship's hold and grant a power-up choice" (epic that introduced the hold-full mechanic).
- **AH-0MUCST2VY004T6QQ** — "Test: Hold-full choice scene and PlayScene wiring" (tests for the choice scene).
- **AH-0MUCST5W9009BH34** — "Documentation and full project test suite validation" (test validation).

Saving ship (or enemy) config from the gym overwrites `src/data/ship-config.csv` with only the header row + data row, dropping the `#` comment block that documents every column, enum values, and how to add entries.

**Why it matters:** the committed CSVs are documented as the "single, human-editable source of truth" (README "Configuration (CSV)"). After the first gym save, the human-readable column documentation is lost, making the file harder to hand-edit.

**Reproduction:** open the Player gym, change any value, click Save. Inspect `src/data/ship-config.csv` — the leading `#` comment lines are gone (see the `M src/data/ship-config.csv` diff on the working tree).

**Suggested approach:** have the dev-server plugin preserve the original comment prefix when rewriting the file, or move the column documentation out of the CSV (e.g. README/schema) so it is not destroyed by writes.

# Add Pages deploy trigger regression test

## Summary

Test-first verifier feature for *GitHub Pages deploy rejects release tags (environment policy allows only dev)* (`AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77`). Adds an automated regression test that pins the **tag-only trigger contract** of `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`, so a future workflow edit cannot silently start deploying on branch pushes or pull requests.

## User story

As a future maintainer, I want an automated test that fails if the Pages deploy workflow starts triggering on non-tag events, so the tag-only release contract is protected without manual YAML review.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criterion **AC4** requires that `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes, and that non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy.
- The workflow currently declares `on.push.tags: ['v*']` and a `deploy` job targeting environment `github-pages`.
- This item is created and completed **before** the environment-policy implementation items (test-first ordering).

## Scope

In scope:

- A hermetic vitest test that reads `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` from the repository root and asserts its trigger shape.

Out of scope:

- Changing the workflow (no change is expected for this fix).
- Calling the live GitHub API.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` still triggers only on `v*` tag pushes; non-tag events (push to `main`/`dev`, pull requests) do not deploy.
- The test asserts the only trigger is `push` with `tags: ['v*']` — no `branches`, no `pull_request`, and no `workflow_dispatch`.
- The test asserts the workflow contains a `deploy` job targeting the `github-pages` environment and a `build` job the deploy needs.
- The test is hermetic (reads only the checked-out workflow file) and runs as part of `npm test` with no new runtime dependency (`npm run build` and `npm test` both pass).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a vitest test (e.g. `scripts/deploy-pages-workflow.test.ts`, or co-located under `src/` if `scripts/` has no test wiring) that reads the workflow file using `node:fs` relative to the repo root.
- Parse the workflow text with focused assertions (regex/string checks or `yaml` if already available transitively); avoid adding a production dependency for a single test.
- Assert: `push.tags` is exactly `['v*']`; no `push.branches`; no `pull_request` / `workflow_dispatch` trigger keys; `jobs.deploy.environment.name == 'github-pages'`.
- Confirm the test is picked up by the existing `vitest.config.ts` include globs; adjust the include pattern only if the file lives outside the current test roots.

## Deliverables

- New automated trigger-contract test.
- `npm test` green including the new test.

## Dependencies

None.

## Key Files

- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` — The workflow whose trigger contract is asserted (no change expected).
- `vitest.config.ts` — Test include globs; may need to cover the new test location.
- `scripts/deploy-pages-workflow.test.ts` — New hermetic regression test.
data.title: Add Pages deploy trigger regression test
